meta.name: Send daily competitor intel briefs to Slack with API Direct and OpenAI

name: Monitor competitors on Twitter/X and Google News with AI briefs in Slack

parameters.content:
## Daily competitor intel brief in Slack

## Who's it for

Product marketers, founders, and competitive intelligence teams who want a daily pulse on a competitor without checking feeds by hand.

## How it works

Every morning the workflow searches Twitter/X and Google News for your competitor's name via API Direct (pay-as-you-go, from $0.002/request) — newest tweets plus articles from the last 24 hours — and drops anything it already covered on a previous run. An AI step then reads all the new mentions and writes a three-bullet intelligence brief: what happened, what people are complaining about, what's worth acting on. The brief plus the source links is posted to a Slack channel as one message — competitor intel before your standup, with receipts.

This template uses the [API Direct](https://apidirect.io) verified community node — available on n8n Cloud and self-hosted n8n (search “API Direct” in the nodes panel). No official API access, developer accounts, or OAuth apps needed.

## How to set up

1. Create an [API Direct](https://apidirect.io) account, copy your API key, and add it as a credential in both search nodes (new accounts include free credit).
2. Add an OpenAI credential to the model node (or swap in any chat model n8n supports).
3. Open **Edit your competitor settings** and set the competitor name.
4. Connect your Slack account and pick the channel.
5. Activate the workflow (the seen-mention memory only persists on active workflows).

## Requirements

- API Direct API key
- An LLM provider credential (OpenAI by default)
- Slack workspace

## How to customize

- Track several competitors by duplicating the flow or looping over a list.
- Use [boolean search syntax](https://apidirect.io/docs/boolean-search) to cut noise: `"Acme" -job -hiring`.
- Add Reddit, TikTok, or YouTube as extra sources with more API Direct nodes.
- Change the brief's angle in the AI prompt — sales ammo, product gaps, or PR risk.

### How it flows
Search newest tweets + last-24h news → drop already-seen mentions → AI writes a 3-bullet intel brief → one Slack message with the brief + source links.

Already-seen results are remembered between runs (n8n workflow static data), so daily runs only process new items. The memory starts working once the workflow is **activated** — manual test runs always process everything.

parameters.text:
=You are a competitive intelligence analyst. Below are today's new mentions of {{ $json.competitor }} from Twitter/X and news.

Write exactly three short bullets:
1. What happened (launches, press, incidents)
2. What users are complaining about or praising
3. What is worth acting on

Be concrete and skip filler. If the mentions are all noise, say so in one line instead.

Mentions:
{{ $json.corpus }}
